note: Team-written summaries of the cited public guidance. Loaded as drafts; a node's expert reviews them before they are published.

practices.title: Broad Bed and Furrow (BBF) on black soils
practices.summary: Raised beds about 1.2-1.5 m wide separated by furrows drain excess water in wet spells and conserve moisture in dry spells on heavy Vertisols.
steps: Form beds with a BBF planter or ridger before sowing, with furrows along a gentle slope.
Sow 2-4 crop rows on each bed; keep furrows unplanted.
Keep furrow outlets open so excess rain drains to a grassed waterway or farm pond.
contraindications: Needs contour bunding on slopes steeper than about 1.5%.
Of little benefit on light sandy soils.

practices.title: Cotton with pigeon pea strip intercropping
practices.summary: Rows of pigeon pea between cotton strips add biological nitrogen, diversify income and break pest build-up in rainfed cotton.
steps: Sow cotton and pigeon pea together at monsoon onset in a 6:1 or 8:2 row ratio.
Keep recommended spacing for each crop so pigeon pea does not shade cotton.
Harvest cotton in pickings; harvest pigeon pea after cotton.
contraindications: Avoid indeterminate climbing pulse varieties that smother cotton.

practices.title: Crop residue mulching instead of burning
practices.summary: Keeping chopped residue on the soil surface cuts evaporation, protects soil from rain impact and feeds soil life; burning destroys organic matter and pollutes the air.
steps: Chop and spread the previous crop's residue evenly.
Sow the next crop with a zero-till or Happy Seeder drill through the residue.
contraindications: Very thick wet mulch on poorly drained soil can encourage seedling rot.

practices.title: No-till on straw (plantio direto)
practices.summary: Sow directly into the previous crop's straw without ploughing, keep the soil covered all year and rotate crops. It cuts erosion, holds soil moisture and builds organic matter; it is the standard grain system in Paraná.
steps: Keep the previous crop's straw on the surface; do not plough or harrow.
Sow with a no-till planter that cuts through the straw.
Follow soybean or maize with a winter cover or grain crop (for example black oat or wheat) so the soil is never bare.
contraindications: Compacted or badly eroded fields may need one-time correction (subsoiling, terracing, liming) before starting.

practices.title: Bradyrhizobium seed inoculation for soybean
practices.summary: Inoculating soybean seed with Bradyrhizobium lets the crop fix most of its own nitrogen, so no nitrogen fertiliser is needed on soybean.
steps: Use a registered Bradyrhizobium inoculant within its expiry date.
Treat seed in the shade just before sowing and sow the same day.
Re-inoculate every season, also in fields where soybean was grown before.
contraindications: Keep inoculant away from seed treatment chemicals that are not compatible; follow the label.
